social.instagram_caption:
That head-rush moment when you stand up too fast — is that normal on tirzepatide?

Here's what the label actually shows:
🌀 Dizziness: 4–5% on tirzepatide vs 2% on placebo
🩸 Low blood pressure: 1–2% on tirzepatide vs 0% on placebo
Both from two 72-week weight trials in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition.

Possible everyday contributors (not a diagnosis):
• Eating much less
• Too little fluid
• Vomiting or diarrhoea
• Standing up fast

Low blood sugar is a higher risk for people with diabetes taking insulin or a sulfonylurea.

Save this for your next "is this normal?" moment 💾

Call your local emergency number right away for fainting, chest pain or confusion. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

#Tirzepatide

factcheck.summary: I checked every number against the live Zepbound label on DailyMed, revised 28 Aug 2026. All of them match. In the pooled Study 1 and Study 2 data (72 weeks), dizziness was 2% on placebo vs 4%, 5% and 4% on the 5, 10 and 15 mg doses. Low blood pressure was 0% on placebo vs 1%, 1% and 2%. The populations are right: Study 1 excluded type 2 diabetes and Study 2 enrolled only people with it. The kidney warning matches the label: most kidney injury events were in people dehydrated by nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea. The low blood sugar warning is correctly limited to people with diabetes taking insulin or an insulin secretagogue such as a sulfonylurea. The safety elements are all present: the emergency line keeps "right away", the scoped don't-stop line is there, there's a line against changing blood pressure medicines alone, and the closing disclaimer is exact. Three minor wording fixes follow. There's nothing misleading or unsafe.

issues.claim: Dizziness was reported by 4–5% on tirzepatide vs 2% on placebo in the weight trials.
issues.problem: The recap leaves out the trial length and population that slide 2 gives. Our rule is that recaps keep the full scope.
issues.fix: Dizziness was reported by 4–5% on tirzepatide vs 2% on placebo in two 72-week weight trials in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

issues.claim: Smaller meals may mean less fuel
issues.problem: The label doesn't say this, and "less fuel" vaguely hints at low blood sugar, which slide 5 correctly limits to people with diabetes on insulin or a sulfonylurea. This slide needs a general-knowledge hedge and must not contradict slide 5.
issues.fix: label: "Eating much less"; detail: "Big drops in intake may leave you feeling low on energy"

issues.claim: Fainting, chest pain or confusion? Call your local emergency number right away.
issues.problem: For chest pain or fainting, our house style puts the emergency action first.
issues.fix: Call your local emergency number right away for fainting, chest pain or confusion. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
